_note: v2 hook overrides for the boulangerie. Every verb is painted as the standard Monsieur Verbe mime (beret color = verb group), so the v1 verb hooks apply unchanged. Other overrides match painted counts/details. v1 data is untouched.

fr_baguette_noun.hook: "ba-GET": a BAG? GET a BAGUETTE! A little girl holds open her paper BAG and GETS a long BAGUETTE from the tall stack; English borrowed the same word.
fr_baguette_noun.why: The old hook had no sound-alike.

fr_sac_noun.hook: A brown paper SACK stuffed with baguettes. Sac sounds just like SACK.
fr_sac_noun.why: The painting shows two baguettes, not three.

fr_panier_noun.hook: A wicker PANNIER full of baguettes on the back of a little bike. A pannier is a basket bag: pannier, panier (pah-NYAY).

fr_plateau_noun.hook: Beside the oven, the baking TRAY sits on the flat top of a little rocky PLATEAU: plah-TOH = plateau.
fr_plateau_noun.why: Painted as a tray resting on a small mesa.

fr_seau_noun.hook: The leaky BUCKET has been SEWN up with big red stitches: SOH = sew.
fr_seau_noun.why: The painted bucket stands by the oven with big red stitches and a needle still in it; the hook names the stitches as the SOH sound.

fr_tablier_noun.hook: A little TABLE wears an APRON with a smiling face and kicks up a leg: "TABLE, YAY!" = tah-blee-YAY.
fr_tablier_noun.why: Matches the painted apron-table, which now stands on its own (the bucket stands behind it by the oven).

fr_boite_noun.hook: The cake BOX has a sail and floats on a puddle like a BOAT: BWAHT = boat.
fr_boite_noun.why: Painted on a puddle on the workbench.

fr_balance_noun.hook: "bah-LAHNS", just like English BALANCE: a BALL of dough and a striped candy stick sit perfectly level on the SCALES.
fr_balance_noun.why: The old hook read the stick as a toy lance (a weapon); it is now a candy stick.

fr_boulanger_noun.hook: "boo-lahn-ZHAY": the jolly BAKER throws up his arms at the oven door: "BOO! LONG DAY!" He has been baking since dawn.
fr_boulanger_noun.why: The old hook needed the French word boulangerie; BOO-LONG-DAY is an English sound-alike.

fr_eclair_noun_2.hook: A chocolate ÉCLAIR pastry with a yellow zigzag of icing like a flash of lightning; a little mouse sniffs it, ready to snatch it in a flash!
fr_eclair_noun_2.why: The mouse was not the hook (it lounged like a person), so it is now a natural mouse on all four paws, and the éclair carries a literal lightning zigzag; same change in the shop painting and in the display-case zoom. RECS 1.4 homograph split: lightning (ciel) vs pastry (bakery).

fr_caisse_noun_2.hook: "KESS": the baker rings up a sale and the till drawer slides out with a ching: the CAISSE (cash register).
fr_caisse_noun_2.why: RECS 1.4 homograph split: crate (maison grenier) vs till (bakery).

fr_four_noun.hook: A baker in a chef's hat waves FOUR ("FOOR") fingers by the brick OVEN.
fr_four_noun.why: RECS double-hooks: one pun per word (matches maison/cuisine); the fur stole on the oven is repainted as a baker holding up four fingers.

fr_viande_noun.hook: A girl carries a big roast VIAND ('vee-AHND', old English for food) on a silver platter.
fr_viande_noun.why: Viand is a real (old) English word for meat/food.

fr_chair_noun.hook: A pink salmon fillet, the fish's FLESH, lies on a little kitchen CHAIR ('shair').
fr_chair_noun.why: Chair = flesh; the chair itself is the sound hook, the fillet the meaning.

fr_saucisse_noun.hook: A string of fresh pink sausages hangs over a SAUCE boat: 'SAUCE-EECE'.
fr_saucisse_noun.why: Fresh links (vs the dried saucisson salami on the right).

fr_carcasse_noun.hook: A whole side of meat, the CARCASS ('kar-KASS'), hangs from a steel hook.

fr_moule_noun_f.hook: A MULE ('mool') peeks in at the window carrying panniers of black MUSSELS.
fr_moule_noun_f.why: Feminine moule = mussel; the mussel panniers are the cue (the toy mule with a cake pan in the worktop is masculine moule = mold).

fr_sardine_noun.hook: An open tin of silver SARDINES ('sar-DEEN').

fr_charcuterie_noun.hook: A SHARK-shaped board ('SHAR-koo-tree') laden with sliced cured meats.
fr_charcuterie_noun.why: The shark is the sound hook for 'shar-'.

fr_galop_noun.hook: A carved wooden horse on the wall, legs outstretched in full GALLOP ('ga-LO').
fr_galop_noun.why: Cognate; mid-gallop pose is the cue.

fr_saucisson_noun.hook: A long dried salami with white bloom hangs on a string, some sliced: 'SAUCE-ee-SON', the big SON of the sausage.
fr_saucisson_noun.why: Dried, sliced salami vs the fresh saucisse links on the left.

fr_saumon_noun.hook: A whole silver SALMON ('so-MON') on ice next to pink salmon steaks.
fr_saumon_noun.why: Pink steaks distinguish it from the plain poisson.

fr_poisson_noun.hook: The butcher's big FISH lies on ice beside an open pod of PEAS: 'PEA-SON' (pois-son).
fr_poisson_noun.why: Plain gray fish + peas; the salmon is the one with pink steaks.

fr_pate_noun_2.hook: A boy PATS the PÂTÉ ('pa-TAY') in its earthenware terrine with his flat palm.
fr_pate_noun_2.why: Masculine pâté (spread), not the feminine pâte (dough) of the display case.

fr_jambon_noun.hook: A whole HAM with a jar of JAM on top: 'JAM-BON'.
fr_jambon_noun.why: Jam jar on the ham is the hook.

fr_porc_noun.hook: Pink PORK chops ('por') on a plate beside a pink piggy bank.

fr_farine_noun.hook: A big sack of FLOUR with a wooden scoop. FARINA, the wheat-flour cereal, says it too: fah-REEN.
fr_farine_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): reworded without "Think of" / "Like English" on a false friend (same painted content).

fr_vendre_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe SELLS a fresh baguette across the counter. A VENDOR VENDS: vendre (VAHN-druh).
fr_vendre_verb.why: Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): reworded without "Think of" / "Like English" on a false friend (same painted content).

fr_moule_noun_m.hook: A MULE wears the cake PAN as a hat: MOOL = mule.
fr_moule_noun_m.why: American words 2026-10-28: the meaning word in capitals changed to its American form (same painting).
